_note: The town's layout and the ground everyone walks on. Plots sit in rings around the hearth (Frostpunk-style): radius = the ring's middle, age = the tech age that opens the ring, ring_depth = how deep a plot is, plot_width = roughly how wide (each ring gets a whole number of plots per sector), sectors = slices of the circle. Plots touch, so a full stretch of ring is a wall; a lane runs between rings. Buildings place themselves on the free plot that suits them (their "near" key in buildings.json), keep off paved road unless nothing else is free (then the stones are lifted and refunded), and never wall off the hearth. obstacles = things already on some plots at the start of a run (count = how many plots). cell = size of a pathfinding square in world units. thickets = patches of scrub out past the town that slow everyone (speed x), radius_min/radius_max = patch size, min_distance = how far from the hearth they start. Desire paths: feet wear the ground by themselves, one stage per dawn. trail = a square walked on for at least traffic seconds (counted up over the days, x decay each dawn) becomes a trail; path = a trail walked on for at least its traffic seconds becomes a worn path; each fades back a stage when walked on less than a quarter of its traffic. roads = what stone-layers pave the busiest worn paths into, best last: a road kind needs its age; each stretch of stretch_cells squares costs cost and takes work craftsperson-seconds. Stone-layers leave keep_in_stock of each good they use, so building orders aren't starved. A building with "paves": true lets craftspeople pave. speed multiplies how fast anyone walks (heroes, townsfolk and raiders alike). gate = how gate buildings (a building with gate_hp) behave: raiders route round a gate when that is shorter than raider_detour squares per point of its health and batter through otherwise; watch posts prefer plots within guard_within of a gate; color = how a standing gate is drawn.

boulder.name: Boulder
boulder.text: A great stone left by the ice. Nothing can be built here and nobody walks through it.

old_oak.name: Old oak
old_oak.text: A huge oak the elders won't let anyone fell. Nothing can be built here and nobody walks through it.

thickets.name: Thicket
thickets.text: Tangled scrub: everyone walks through it at 60% speed. Feet can wear a trail through it.

trail.name: Trail
trail.text: Worn by feet: anyone on it walks 20% faster. Trails form where people walk most and fade where they stop.

path.name: Worn path
path.text: A trail worn deep by many feet: anyone on it walks 35% faster. Stone-layers pave the busiest ones.

stone_path.name: Stone path
stone_path.text: Flat stones laid by the stone-layers on a busy worn path: anyone on it walks 45% faster, raiders too.

cobbled_road.name: Cobbled road
cobbled_road.text: Bronze-age cobbles with a kerb: anyone on it walks 70% faster, raiders too. Stone-layers re-lay old stone paths as cobbles.

flagstone_street.name: Flagstone street
flagstone_street.text: Medieval flagstones with a gutter: anyone on it walks 90% faster, raiders too. Stone-layers re-lay older roads as flagstones.
